title: The Tate endpoint for every unit-normalized equivariant realization
statement: For any supplied realization Data [def-sf-coefficient-realization-cohomology-data] and natural d, degree -2d pair cohomology of the canonical shifted Tate constant pair [def-sf-coefficient-endpoint-objects] is isomorphic to the native d-th Tate sheaf tensor the native constant. No exceptional adjunction, existence of a realization, or smoothness is part of this assertion.

source.place: Final exceptional-adjunction paragraph, combined with exact cohomology and the canonical constant/Tate source of the smooth dualizing specialization.

proof.text: Trivialize the geometric root line using compatible roots. Its Frobenius is q^(-d) on the d-th power. The canonical tensor and pullback unit maps identify the unshifted source with the unit with this scalar action. Changes of root basis commute with that scalar.

source.place: Final exceptional-adjunction paragraph, combined with exact cohomology and the canonical constant/Tate source of the smooth dualizing specialization.

proof.text: Additivity preserves multiplication by q^d and its inverse, hence q^(-d). Naturality and the unit comparison identify the realized pair with the native Tate tensor constant pair. Shift compatibility of the functor and its Frobenius comparison transports the even shift. The single-homology isomorphism in degree -2d yields the stated endpoint, including d=0 and the empty scheme.

theorem realized_tate_cohomology (R : CoefficientRealization.Data P X₀) (d : ℕ) :
    Nonempty
      ((CoefficientRealization.pairCohomology P X₀ R (-2 * (d : ℤ))).obj
          (twistedConstant P X₀ d) ≅
        ((WeilSheaf.tateTwistSheaf P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left d).tensorObj
          (WeilSheaf.adicConstant P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left)
          (WeilSheaf.isLisse_tateTwistSheaf P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left d)).obj)
